title: Speed Dot contested power-up v1
problem_statement: Plan a small, reversible, testable Speed Dot v1: a single contested neutral power-up that grants identical temporary speed boost to Pi-chan or one eligible onion.
game_flow_context: movement / onion pressure / chase eligibility / collision pickup / visual feedback / fixed arena waves
validated_decisions: Speed Dot is a contested neutral opportunity/threat, not a passive player-only bonus.
V1 allows maximum one active Speed Dot.
Boost duration and multiplier must be identical for Pi-chan and onion.
Only one non-chase onion, the nearest to the dot, may target it.
Onions in CHASE_PICHAN must not abandon Pi-chan for the dot.
No aggregation, HP increase, big onion, enemy variant, boost stacking, numeric UI, combo, scoring redesign, or broad refactor.
No code implementation is approved in this orchestrator pass.
LOG-002 gameplay-programmer implementation spec is accepted for regression/impact review.
Pi-chan Speed Dot boost affects movement only and must not increase bullet speed.
Speed Dot v1 remains singleton, no-stack, and limited to one onion candidate.
js/ai/OnionAI.js is forbidden for v1 unless task-orchestrator explicitly reopens it after impact review.
LOG-004 impact-regression-guard approved the build gate with conditions: preserve Player.speed baseline, onion boost as final movement multiplier, atomic consume, LevelManager lifecycle owner.
Speed Dot v1 is approved for build only within main.js, js/core/LevelManager.js, js/entities/Player.js, js/entities/Onion.js; config/levels.json remains optional for one top-level speedDot object.
LOG-006 build-agent report is accepted as BUILD_DONE for maintainability review.
Build changed only approved runtime files: main.js, js/core/LevelManager.js, js/entities/Player.js, js/entities/Onion.js.
Browser gameplay checklist was not executed in LOG-006 and remains review/validation risk.
DONE is accepted with residual notes: browser gameplay checklist not executed; if nearest winner is already boosted, dot remains active instead of selecting another candidate.
validated_facts: main.js owns the central update/draw loop and current collision ordering.
LevelManager owns level reset, player/onion/arena construction, wave state, onion list, queued onion spawning, and wave completion.
config/levels.json contains fixed static arena wave tuning and no power-up settings.
Player.js uses this.speed for movement and derives bullet speed from this.speed when shooting.
Onion.js owns random movement, chase movement, arena constraint, death fade, and onion rendering.
OnionAI.js owns ONION_STATE, shoot-triggered chase, cooldown, and base speed/color recalculation.
No existing power-up system or temporary effect abstraction was found.
No package.json, PHP files, composer.json, or PHPMD config were found.
draft_assumptions_in_play: Speed Dot v1 can be drawn directly on canvas without new assets.
Speed Dot v1 should be enabled for all existing waves unless tuning analysis narrows it.
A small singleton state in LevelManager is preferable to a generic power-up framework for v1.
The gameplay-programmer must explicitly decide whether Pi-chan boost should also increase bullet speed, because current Player.shoot derives bullet speed from player speed.
Candidate targeting can be implemented without modifying chase constants or the OnionAI state machine.
current_direction: Closed DONE after human-supplied review-maintainability-guard verdict APPROVE_WITH_NOTES.
Speed Dot v1 was built as a singleton contested power-up with no stack and one eligible onion candidate.
Runtime implementation stayed within approved files.
Residual notes remain accepted for follow-up awareness: browser gameplay checklist was not executed; winner-already-boosted leaves dot active.
explicit_non_goals: No combo or complex scoring mechanics.
No code outside approved impact surface.
candidate_impact_surface: config/levels.json optional only for one top-level speedDot tuning object
optional_impact_surface: config/levels.json only for one optional top-level speedDot tuning object if impact-regression-guard approves
forbidden_files: js/ai/OnionAI.js unless explicitly reopened by task-orchestrator
docs/** except optional final build/report artifacts
backward_compatibility_concerns: Existing LevelManager config consumers must keep working when speedDot fields are absent.
main.js collision ordering must prevent double pickup while preserving bullet/player, bullet/onion, onion/player, and onion/onion behavior.
Player.speed currently affects both movement and bullet speed at shoot time; LOG-002 requires movement-only Pi-chan boost so bullet speed remains baseline.
OnionAI and Onion chase logic repeatedly recompute onion.speed, so boost reset must not rely on one-time mutation only.
Onion dodge/random movement and dot targeting can conflict if ownership order is unclear.
Reset, Continue, goto, and level transitions must clear dot and boost state.
required_validations: JSON parse for config/levels.json if changed.
Do not change js/ai/OnionAI.js in v1; if later reopened and changed, run node --input-type=module --check < js/ai/OnionAI.js.
Manual browser checklist for dot spawn, pickup, boost, target reassignment, reset, level transition, and wave regression.
PHPMD not applicable unless PHP/config appears in a later task.
human_test_checklist: Wave 1 spawns one Speed Dot after 5-8 seconds.
Pi-chan pickup consumes dot and applies visible 3s speed boost.
A single nearest non-chase onion targets active dot.
Assigned onion pickup consumes dot and applies the same boost duration/multiplier.
Onions in chase keep chasing Pi-chan and ignore dot.
Assigned onion entering chase loses dot target and the dot is reassigned if eligible onion exists.
If all onions are in chase, dot remains only collectible by Pi-chan.
Boost ends and normal speed returns for Pi-chan and onion.
A dot cannot be collected by two subjects in one lifecycle.
Boosted subject has readable visual feedback.
Wave cap, replacement cadence, completion, scoring, bullets, reset, Continue, and goto remain stable.
solution_applied: Speed Dot v1 implemented in approved runtime files: main.js, js/core/LevelManager.js, js/entities/Player.js, js/entities/Onion.js.
LevelManager owns singleton Speed Dot lifecycle, default tuning, spawn/respawn, target assignment, target cleanup, and atomic consume.
main.js integrates Speed Dot update, pickup resolution, and canvas draw inside the existing game loop.
Player boost is movement-only and keeps Player.speed baseline so bullet speed and OnionAI speed through player.speed remain unchanged.
Onion boost is implemented as a final movement multiplier; chase remains dominant over dot targeting.
No config, OnionAI, Bullet, Engine, Arena, physics, asset, sound, CSS, UI/service/network/app, README, or docs runtime changes were accepted.
Static JS checks and server smoke passed per LOG-006.
Task closed DONE with review verdict APPROVE_WITH_NOTES; residual notes recorded.
